title: Developer Audit Handoff & Compliance Evidence Kit for Customer Model Rollouts
author: Aisha M. Turner
body:
Overview:

This page defines a practical, developer-facing "Minimal Evidence Kit" and a step-by-step "Audit Handoff" procedure used when rolling customer-facing model versions (hosted, dedicated, or private). It covers RBAC expectations, required audit events and retention markers, data residency signposts, secure-SDLC gate checks, incident-response readiness, and a compact evidence package format that satisfies our common compliance requests (SOC2/ISO/enterprise customers).

Goals:
- Give engineering teams a concrete checklist so compliance artifacts are produced automatically or with a single command.
- Reduce friction in post-release audits and incident investigations.
- Standardize what counts as "sufficient evidence" for common risk exceptions.

Audience:
- Backend and runtime engineers doing model rollouts
- Release managers and SREs
- Security and compliance reviewers

Quick summary (one-line):
Provide the Minimal Evidence Kit (log bundle + RBAC snapshot + residency manifest + release checklist) and run the Audit Handoff script prior to a customer-facing rollout.

1) Minimal Evidence Kit (what must be produced)

Produce the following artifacts and include them in the evidence bundle. Artifacts should be uploaded to the secure evidence store with prefix: evidence/<team>/<release-id>/

- RBAC snapshot (rbac-snapshot.json): current role bindings for service-accounts and human principals with timestamps.
- Audit event sample (audit-sample.ndjson): 7-day rolling sample of relevant events (authz decisions, token issuance, model-invocation start/end, rollback, configuration changes).
- Release manifest (release-manifest.yaml): model version, pinned quantization profile, rollout policy (canary %, routes), target region(s).
- Residency manifest (residency-manifest.json): dataset regions, inference-data residency markers, encrypted-at-rest flags, KMS key identifiers.
- SDLC gate proof (gate-proofs.md): short list of completed security gates and corresponding ticket/PR IDs.
- Incident-response readiness (ir-checklist.txt): on-call rotation, escalation chain, forensic contact, and retention key.
- Evidence index (index.json): short index listing files, sha256 checksums, and canonical timestamps.

ASCII table: Minimal Evidence Kit contents

| filename | purpose | retention target | owner |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| rbac-snapshot.json | Authorizations at release time | 3 years | identity-team |
| audit-sample.ndjson | Representative audit events | 1 year (sampled), full stream per policy | infra-logging |
| release-manifest.yaml | Deployment configuration | lifecycle of model + 1 year | runtime-team |
| residency-manifest.json | Residency flags and descriptors | 5 years (customer-specific) | data-governance |
| gate-proofs.md | Evidence of SDLC gates | 3 years | product-security |
| ir-checklist.txt | Incident readiness notes | 1 year | eng-sre |
| index.json | Manifest and checksums | 5 years | security |

2) RBAC and auth expectations (developer checklist)

- Use scoped service accounts for deployments; no long-lived human tokens should be embedded in manifest artifacts.
- Run `rbac-dump --release <id> --format json > rbac-snapshot.json` prior to promotion. Ensure all bindings include an `expires_at` or `granted_at` timestamp.
- Default role-to-resource mappings for model-serving (minimal):
  - model-deployer: can create/modify release-manifests, trigger rollouts
  - model-operator: can change routing/scale, cannot modify model artifacts
  - incident-first-responder: read access to logs and ability to create incident artifacts
  - observability-reader: read-only dashboards and traces

3) Audit logging contract (events and schema)

- Minimum events that must be present in the audit-sample.ndjson: AUTHN_LOGIN, AUTHZ_DECISION, MODEL_INVOKE_START, MODEL_INVOKE_END, MODEL_ROLLOUT, CONFIG_CHANGE, SECRET_ACCESS (when KMS keys are referenced), DEPLOYMENT_ROLLBACK, INCIDENT_CREATE.
- Each event should include the following top-level fields: timestamp, event_type, principal_id, principal_type, resource, resource_id, decision (allow/deny), reason, request_id, region, retention_marker.

Example NDJSON event (single line):
{
  "timestamp": "2027-02-01T14:32:05Z",
  "event_type": "MODEL_INVOKE_START",
  "principal_id": "svc-runtime-23",
  "principal_type": "service_account",
  "resource": "model-inference",
  "resource_id": "m-yellowbird-v2",
  "request_id": "req-9a8f",
  "region": "eu-west-1",
  "decision": "allow",
  "reason": "within-quotas",
  "retention_marker": "policy:standard-1yr"
}

- Sampling guidance: when full-stream retention is not feasible, include a deterministic sample keyed on request_id hash (e.g., 1:100 sample) and always include events that are CONFIG_CHANGE or MODEL_ROLLOUT.

4) Data residency & retention signposts

- residency-manifest.json must explicitly list: primary_data_region, secondary_data_region (if any), residency_policy_id, customer_residency_constraints.
- If any inference payload touches customer-controlled PII, include a `pii_present` boolean and pointer to the de-identification artifact.
- Retention banner: provide an `evidence-retention-schedule.txt` that maps each artifact to a retention policy id (e.g., standard-1yr, extended-5yr-customerA).

5) Secure SDLC gates (pre-rollout checklist)

Run and record the following tasks before handing off evidence:
1. Security code scan (SAST) run and findings triaged. Link to ticket IDs in gate-proofs.md.
2. Dependency risk check produced (SBOM snapshot included).
3. Model evaluation for safety regressions: include eval ID and test-set hashes.
4. Secrets/keys: ensure keys referenced in release-manifest use KMS key IDs, not raw secrets.
5. Canary plan: percent, duration, rollback criteria documented.

6) Incident-response tie-ins (how to package evidence quickly)

- When an incident is declared, create an evidence bundle using the same index format. The incident lead runs: `evidence-assemble --release <id> --since <ts> --out /tmp/evidence-bundle` which produces index.json.
- For high-severity incidents (P1/P0), escalate to legal and compliance immediately and set `confidentiality: restricted` for the bundle.
- Preserve the full raw audit stream for the timeframe of the incident; sampled artifacts can be used for non-critical postmortems.

7) Compliance evidence workflow (who does what)

- Runtime team: assembles release-manifest, residency-manifest, runs rbac-dump.
- Infra-logging: extracts audit-sample and verifies schema compliance.
- Security: reviews gate-proofs and the index.json, approves evidence upload.
- Product-security / Compliance: final sign-off for customer disclosures and regulatory artifacts.

Approval flow (numbered):
1. Developer/owner triggers evidence pack script.
2. Infra-logging validates sample and annotates with retention markers.
3. Security performs a light review (24h SLA) and either approves or requests remediation.
4. Compliance signs off (48h SLA for routine rollouts).

8) Risk exceptions and short-form waivers

When a required artifact cannot be produced (e.g., legacy private deployment where logging is partial), follow the exception process:
- Create an exception request with: release-id, missing-artifact, compensating control, mitigation plan, expires_at.
- Tag the request with an initial risk score (low/medium/high) and assign to a risk owner.
- Compensating controls may include increased sampling, extended retention, additional manual attestations, or on-site audit support.
- Exception approval must include signatures from the runtime owner, security, and the compliance manager.

Template: exception request (short)
- release_id: R-2027-01-55
- missing_artifact: full audit stream
- compensating_control: 30-day raw export and extended sampling; manual attest signed by eng lead
- mitigation_deadline: 2027-03-01
- risk_owner: runtime-owner@example.redwood.com

9) Packaging the evidence for external auditors (format & transfer)

- Preferred format: ZIP with index.json at the root and each artifact in a named folder. Attach SHA256 for each file in index.json.
- Transfer: use secure SFTP to the auditor or place in ephemeral secure-share with an audit access grant. Document transfer in evidence index with `transfer_method` and `transfer_timestamp`.

10) Operational playbook snippets (commands)

- Produce RBAC snapshot:
  rbac-dump --env prod --release R-2027-01-55 --format json > rbac-snapshot.json

- Export audit sample for a time window (requires infra-logging role):
  audit-export --start 2027-01-25T00:00:00Z --end 2027-02-01T00:00:00Z --filter "event_type in (MODEL_ROLLOUT,CONFIG_CHANGE,MODEL_INVOKE_START,MODEL_INVOKE_END)" > audit-sample.ndjson

- Assemble evidence bundle:
  evidence-assemble --release R-2027-01-55 --include rbac,release,logs,residency --out /tmp/evidence-bundle.zip

11) Ownership, SLAs and contact matrix

- identity-team: RBAC snapshots; SLA 1 business day for ad-hoc requests.
- infra-logging: audit exports; SLA 4 hours for P1, 24 hours for routine exports.
- runtime-team: release manifest and rollout metadata; SLA immediate on release.
- security: review evidence; SLA 24 hours for routine, 4 hours for P1.

12) Example index.json (short)
{
  "release_id": "R-2027-01-55",
  "files": [
    {"path": "rbac-snapshot.json", "sha256": "<hash>", "size": "14KB"},
    {"path": "audit-sample.ndjson", "sha256": "<hash>", "size": "3MB"}
  ],
  "created_by": "svc-runtime-23",
  "created_at": "2027-02-01T15:00:00Z"
}

References and links:
- See policy: internal://security/evidence-retention (internal retention matrix)
- Audit schema: ../audit-logging/event-schema-contract-and-retention-runbook-2025.json
- RBAC tools: internal://identity/rbac-cli

Appendix A — common failure modes and mitigations:
- Missing timestamps in RBAC snapshot: reject bundle; require re-run with `--include-timestamps`.
- Incomplete log schema: infra-logging to auto-inject `retention_marker` during export.
- Residency unclear: block rollout until tenancy and KMS ownership are defined or raise a risk exception.

Appendix B — FAQ (short)
Q: Who can request ad-hoc evidence for an audit?
A: Security, Compliance, Legal, or a verified auditor with a documented request ticket.

Q: What if logs contain PII?
A: Use the de-identification pipeline and include the de-id proof in the bundle; mark residency-manifest accordingly.
